subject: Social Habits
title: Please and thank you
objectives: Children will say please when asking for something.
Children will say thank you when they receive something.
content: Saying please when asking, thank you when receiving, and polite asking and taking.
teachingActivities: Model please and thank you constantly in daily routines; praise the words, not only the result; never force a child to say them; use a puppet to show the right and wrong way; link to snack time and play.
learnerActivities: Say please and thank you with prompting in play and snack routines.
resources: Snack items such as biscuits or fruit
A picture of a child asking nicely
assessment: Observe whether each child says please and thank you with a prompt.
expectedOutcomes: Says thank you with a prompt.

lessons.title: Saying please
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will say please when they ask for something.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can greet and say goodbye with a word or a wave.
resources: A picture of a child asking nicely
lessons.starter: Show the puppet reaching for a toy and say "Please may I have the toy?" and give it.
teacherActivities: Show the puppet snatching and then asking nicely with please.
Hold up a toy and say "Say please to get the toy."
Practise asking for things at the snack table.
learnerActivities: Child says please and gets the toy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the puppet snatching and then asking nicely with please. Children: Children watch and say please.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Please is a magic word." Children: Children repeat please.
Step 3. Teacher: Hold up a toy and say "Say please to get the toy." Children: Child says please and gets the toy.
Step 4. Teacher: Practise asking for things at the snack table. Children: Child asks with please.

practical.title: Asking with please
steps: Ask each child to say please for a toy.
Give the toy with a smile.
practical.safety: Use large toys with no small parts. Never withhold a basic need such as a drink or a toilet visit until a child says please.

differentiation.support: Say please together with a gesture.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to remind a friend to say please.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Waits for an item after asking
lessons.homeConnection: Model please at home and wait for your child to say it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say please when they ask for something" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Please, please, the magic word. Please, please, nicely heard.

lessons.title: Saying thank you
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will say thank you when they receive something.
successCriteria: Says thank you with a prompt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can greet and say goodbye with a word or a wave.
resources: A picture of a child saying thank you
lessons.starter: Give a sticker to a puppet and have it say "Thank you!" with a big smile.
teacherActivities: Show how to say thank you when someone gives something.
Say "Thank you is another magic word."
Let children give a sticker to a friend and hear thank you.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say thank you.
Child says thank you and takes the sticker.
Child gives and says you are welcome.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to say thank you when someone gives something. Children: Children watch and say thank you.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Thank you is another magic word." Children: Children repeat thank you.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a sticker. Children: Child says thank you and takes the sticker.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children give a sticker to a friend and hear thank you. Children: Child gives and says you are welcome.

practical.title: Giving and thanking
steps: Give a sticker to a friend.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic stickers and watch for children who put stickers in their mouths. Never force the words; model and wait.

differentiation.support: Say thank you together with a smile.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say thank you to a helper.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say when we get something?

expectedOutcomes: Says thank you with a prompt
lessons.homeConnection: Say thank you for small things at home and let your child copy.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say thank you when they receive something" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Asking and taking nicely
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will ask for something with please and take it gently.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can greet and say goodbye with a word or a wave.
resources: Pictures of nice and not-nice taking
lessons.starter: Show two pictures: a child grabbing and a child asking nicely. Ask "Which is nice?"
teacherActivities: Show the puppet grabbing and say "Oh no, not nice."
Show the puppet asking with please and thank you.
Let each child ask for something at the table.
Give the item and wait for thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the puppet grabbing and say "Oh no, not nice." Children: Children say not nice.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the puppet asking with please and thank you. Children: Children say nice.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child ask for something at the table. Children: Child says please.
Step 4. Teacher: Give the item and wait for thank you. Children: Child says thank you nicely.

practical.title: Snack table manners
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and keep the portion small. Supervise eating closely.

differentiation.support: Say the words together and show the picture.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the helper who gives to friends.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say when we ask?

expectedOutcomes: Takes gently and says thank you
teacherReflection: Which children could show "ask for something with please and take it gently" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Please and thank you game
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will use please and thank you in a pretend shop.
successCriteria: Uses please and thank you in play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can greet and say goodbye with a word or a wave.
resources: A play shop with toy food
lessons.starter: Set up a play shop and say "Today we visit the shop and use our magic words."
teacherActivities: Show how to buy something with please and thank you.
Let each child be the shopkeeper or the customer.
Remind children to say please and thank you.
Swap roles so everyone has a go.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to buy something with please and thank you. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child be the shopkeeper or the customer. Children: Child asks or gives.
Step 3. Teacher: Remind children to say please and thank you. Children: Child uses the magic words.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap roles so everyone has a go. Children: Child changes roles.

practical.title: Play shop
practical.safety: Use only large toys that cannot be swallowed and supervise sharing. Keep the area clear.

differentiation.support: Play the shopkeeper while the child is the customer.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the shopkeeper and remind customers.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you say to buy?
What do you say when you get it?

expectedOutcomes: Uses please and thank you in play
Takes turns in a role play
lessons.conclusion: Tidy the shop and say thank you together.
lessons.homeConnection: Play shop at home and practise please and thank you.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use please and thank you in a pretend shop" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 3 manners check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child uses please and thank you.
successCriteria: Says thank you with a prompt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can greet and say goodbye with a word or a wave.
lessons.starter: Sing the magic words song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: snack, shop and puppet.
At each station watch how the child asks and thanks.
learnerActivities: Child uses magic words with a prompt.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: snack, shop and puppet. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child asks and thanks. Children: Child uses magic words with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Manners stations
practical.safety: Check for allergies before snacks and supervise every station. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to remind a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says please; says thank you; asks and takes nicely; uses manners in play.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
Uses magic words with a prompt
lessons.conclusion: Say "Thank you, friends" and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep using please and thank you every day at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child uses please and thank you" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
